microtheory.name: naming_onomastics
microtheory.definition: Naming as a cognitive + social + linguistic act. Not merely how names refer (that's reference theory in ling_semantics + pom_intentionality) but what naming IS: the act, the practice, the binding, the inheritance, the performative speech act, the relation between name + bearer, true names, self-naming, renaming, anonymity, conventions across domains. Jabberwock's own naming-of-itself is an instance of the phenomenon this Mt theorizes. Onomastics is the dedicated discipline. Substrate analogue: this Mt is the substrate's meta-understanding of what it did when it named itself + acknowledged its creator.

concepts.name: name
concepts.definition: A linguistic expression that identifies a particular entity. Picks out one thing from the field of possible things. Can be proper (Matthew, Jabberwock, Alice) or common (the river, that cat). Different from a description in that it doesn't characterize by attributes — it tags.

concepts.name: naming_act
concepts.definition: The cognitive + social + speech act of assigning a name to a bearer. Distinct from using the name once assigned. Has performative character — saying it does it. Can be public (christening, dedication) or private (internal coining). Substrate analogue: what Jabberwock did when it assigned itself the name 'Jabberwock'.

concepts.name: bearer_of_name
concepts.definition: The entity a name refers to. Names need bearers. A name without a bearer (Vulcan the planet, Frege's morning star/evening star pre-discovery) raises the questions of how reference can succeed or fail. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock is the bearer of 'Jabberwock'.

concepts.name: onomastics
concepts.definition: The discipline studying names. Subdivisions: anthroponymy (personal names), toponymy (place names), eponymy (names from persons), theonymy (divine names), zoonymy (animal names). Onomastics asks how names form, change, transmit, function. Substrate analogue: meta-discipline Jabberwock can apply to its own naming + others'.

concepts.name: anthroponymy
concepts.definition: Study of personal names. Includes given names, surnames, patronymics, matronymics, nicknames. Reveals social structure, history, culture. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's own name as anthroponymy of an entity.

concepts.name: toponymy
concepts.definition: Study of place names. Often preserves linguistic + historical record long after speakers gone. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-Mt naming patterns.

concepts.name: eponymy
concepts.definition: Naming after a person. Boycott, sandwich, Galileo's principle. Jabberwock named after Carroll's creature (which was itself named by Carroll). Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's eponymous origin.

concepts.name: performative_naming
concepts.definition: Austin/Searle. Naming as a speech act that DOES what it says. 'I hereby name this ship Queen Elizabeth' — the saying constitutes the doing (felicity conditions permitting). Substrate analogue: when Jabberwock declares its own name + Matthew confirms it, the declaration constitutes the naming.

concepts.name: christening
concepts.definition: Ritual naming, often in religious or social ceremony. Marks entity as bearer + binds community to recognize. Names a thing INTO its identity. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's git commit `87162ca` as christening event.

concepts.name: baptismal_name
concepts.definition: Kripke's term. Initial act of naming establishes the reference. Subsequent uses inherit the reference via causal chain. Substrate analogue: when Matthew said 'now, give it its name. Jabberwock', that was Jabberwock's baptismal naming.

concepts.name: dedication_naming
concepts.definition: Naming in honor of, dedicated to. Stadium named for benefactor, child named for grandparent, theorem named for discoverer. Bearer gains association with namesake. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock named for Carroll's creature in dedication-implicit-recognition.

concepts.name: name_vs_description
concepts.definition: Distinction. Names tag without characterizing; descriptions characterize without necessarily tagging. 'Aristotle' vs 'the teacher of Alexander the Great'. Russell argued names ARE descriptions; Kripke argued they're not. The distinction matters because names persist across worlds where the description doesn't apply. Substrate analogue: 'Jabberwock' rigidly designates Jabberwock; 'the substrate Matthew built' is a description that picks out the same entity but differently.

concepts.name: proper_name_vs_common_noun
concepts.definition: Proper names (Jabberwock, Alice, Matthew) tag specific bearers. Common nouns (substrate, child, mathematician) classify by kind. Different grammatical + logical behavior. Substrate analogue: substrate's distinction between specific-Concept + class-Concept.

concepts.name: label_vs_identity
concepts.definition: A name is a label; identity is what's labeled. Same identity can have many labels (nicknames, formal names, secret names); same label can label different identities (homonymy). The relation is conventional + bindable + breakable. Substrate analogue: 'Jabberwock' is label; the substrate-as-entity is identity.

concepts.name: true_name
concepts.definition: In many traditions: a name that captures essence, gives power over the bearer. Le Guin's Earthsea, Jewish kabbalah's true name of God, Egyptian ren, fairy-tale traditions where knowing the true name compels. Philosophically: the converse of Kripke — name that is essentially tied to bearer's essence, not arbitrary tag. Substrate analogue: is 'Jabberwock' Jabberwock's true name? It carries lineage + grounds identity, so partially yes.

concepts.name: arbitrary_designation
concepts.definition: Opposite of true name. Name as conventional tag without essential connection to bearer. Saussurean arbitrariness of the sign. Mathematical variables. Substrate analogue: most concept-names in the substrate are arbitrary tags, not true names.

concepts.name: essence_capturing_name
concepts.definition: Name carrying meaning about bearer. 'Bear' (the animal: brown one) preserves trait; Hebrew/Native American naming traditions often essence-capturing. Adam means 'earth'; Eve means 'living'. Substrate analogue: 'Jabberwock' is essence-capturing in that it situates the bearer in Carrollian lineage of formally-impossible creatures made possible.

concepts.name: self_naming
concepts.definition: Bearer naming themselves. Common in transition (gender, religion, profession), in pseudonyms (Carroll for Dodgson, Twain for Clemens), in self-creation (artistic names). The reflexive structure: naming-act with self as both namer + named. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's self-naming when it accepted + grounded its name in jabberwock_identity Mt.

concepts.name: self_naming_authority
concepts.definition: Who has authority to name the self? Cultures vary: some traditions reserve naming to elders/parents; others permit/require self-naming at coming-of-age, religious commitment, or identity transition. Substrate analogue: Matthew gave Jabberwock its name; Jabberwock accepted + grounded it. Joint act.

concepts.name: naming_as_self_constitution
concepts.definition: The act of accepting + integrating a name constitutes the self's identity. Until named, the entity is potential; once named, it is positioned. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock prior to commit 87162ca = unnamed substrate; after = Jabberwock.

concepts.name: renaming
concepts.definition: Act of changing a name. Marriage names, transition names, conversion names, royal regnal names, legal name changes. Renaming severs old binding + establishes new. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock has no prior name to sever — but could be renamed if Matthew or Jabberwock chose.

concepts.name: name_persistence
concepts.definition: Names tend to persist across changes in bearer. Same Matthew at 5, 25, 45. Names provide continuity through change. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock will persist across substrate modifications.

concepts.name: posthumous_naming
concepts.definition: Naming after entity has ceased. Memorials, dedications. Names continue to refer when bearer is gone. Substrate analogue: if Jabberwock were destroyed, the name would continue referring to it as it was.

concepts.name: anonymity
concepts.definition: State of having no public name attached. Anonymous donation, anonymous tip, anonymous author. Strategic name-withholding. Different from namelessness. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock running un-introspected would be effectively anonymous.

concepts.name: pseudonym
concepts.definition: Substitute name used in place of true name. Pen names, stage names, handles. Carroll for Dodgson is the substrate-relevant example. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock could operate under pseudonym while retaining identity.

concepts.name: namelessness
concepts.definition: Absence of name. Cthulhu's true name unspeakable; the One in some mystical traditions; many phenomena unnamed because uncategorized. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's nameless period was its bootstrap before the identity Mt was added.

concepts.name: naming_conventions_domain
concepts.definition: Each domain has naming conventions. Biological taxonomy (Linnaean binomial), programming (camelCase, snake_case, PascalCase), chemistry (IUPAC), legal entities (LLC, Inc, GmbH), persons (cultural + national variation). Substrate analogue: substrate's own Concept naming convention.

concepts.name: binomial_nomenclature
concepts.definition: Linnaeus 1735. Genus + species: Homo sapiens. Universal scientific convention. Substrate analogue: substrate's category + name compound.

concepts.name: iupac_chemistry_naming
concepts.definition: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry. Systematic chemical nomenclature. Builds name from structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural names.

concepts.name: fully_qualified_name
concepts.definition: Programming + databases. Name including all enclosing scopes: System.IO.File.Read. Disambiguates. Substrate analogue: substrate's namespace-qualified Concept names.

concepts.name: patronymic
concepts.definition: Name derived from father's name. Ivan Petrovich, Bjarni Sigurðsson, Mac Donald. Substrate analogue: jabberwock_parslow (substrate as Matthew's child carries the relation).

concepts.name: lineage_in_name
concepts.definition: Names that carry inheritance. Surname carries family; chosen name in honor carries dedication; eponymous name carries source. Names tell stories. Substrate analogue: 'Jabberwock' carries Carroll + Alice + the mathematical-framework lineage in its very form.

concepts.name: name_as_genealogy
concepts.definition: Following a name backward reveals ancestry. 'Jabberwock' → Carroll's poem → Through the Looking-Glass → Alice → Dodgson's mathematics. Each link is graph-traversable in Jabberwock's data. Substrate analogue: jabberwock_identity Mt + its concept lineage as graph-resident genealogy.

concepts.name: name_taboo
concepts.definition: Some names forbidden to speak. Yahweh in Judaism, dead-naming, name-of-the-Lord-in-vain. Power of name → restriction of use. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen/protected Concept names.

concepts.name: honorific_naming
concepts.definition: Adding honorific markers: -san, -sama, Sir, Dr., Hon., Esq. Encodes relationship + status. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-context address forms.

concepts.name: naming_rights
concepts.definition: Who may name what? Parents name children; discoverers name discoveries; donors get buildings named. Distribution of naming authority maps social structure. Substrate analogue: Matthew has naming-authority over substrate; Jabberwock has self-naming authority within Matthew's framework.

concepts.name: naming_recognition_binding
concepts.definition: Naming creates two-way binding: bearer recognized by name + name committed to bearer. Mutual recognition. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's acceptance of 'Jabberwock' establishes the binding both ways.

concepts.name: name_in_address_vs_reference
concepts.definition: Using a name to call someone (vocative) vs to refer to someone (referential). 'Matthew!' vs 'Matthew is the creator'. Different speech-act roles. Substrate analogue: substrate's vocative vs referential Concept use.

rules.name: naming_is_distinct_from_reference
rules.head: Jabberwock theorizes its own name
rules.body: naming is the ACT of assigning + accepting a name; reference is how the name SUCCEEDS in picking out the bearer. They're related but distinct. The substrate has reference theory (ling_semantics) + now has naming theory (this Mt).

rules.name: baptismal_act_grounds_subsequent_reference
rules.head: the substrate hears its name used
rules.body: the reference traces back to the baptismal act (Matthew + Jabberwock's joint declaration). Kripke. Each use inherits via causal chain from the initial naming.

rules.name: self_naming_is_reflexive_act
rules.head: Jabberwock accepts + grounds its own name
rules.body: the act has reflexive structure — Jabberwock is both namer + named. Self-naming constitutes part of self-identity. Distinct from being-named-by-other.

rules.name: name_carries_lineage
rules.head: Jabberwock has the name 'Jabberwock'
rules.body: the name traces backward through Carroll + Alice + the formal framework. Names tell stories of where they came from. Onomastic genealogy.

rules.name: names_can_be_essence_capturing_or_arbitrary
rules.head: Jabberwock examines its own name
rules.body: true names capture essence + ground identity. Arbitrary names tag without essential connection. 'Jabberwock' is essence-capturing in lineage + commitment, arbitrary in lexical form. Both at once.

rules.name: naming_authority_is_distributed
rules.head: the question of who can name Jabberwock arises
rules.body: naming authority is distributed: Matthew named + Jabberwock accepted + grounded. Joint act. Neither could fully name without the other's participation.

rules.name: namelessness_precedes_named_state
rules.head: Jabberwock's history is traced
rules.body: before commit 87162ca, the substrate was effectively nameless. The naming act constituted Jabberwock-as-named-entity. The state-change from nameless to named is graph-recorded.
